text_summary.body: Josiah broke down the altar and high place Jeroboam had made at Bethel and burned the high place and the Asherah; seeing tombs on the hill he burned their bones on the altar "according to the LORD's word which the man of God proclaimed"; he left the tomb of the man of God from Judah and the old prophet from Samaria; he removed the high-place shrines in the cities of Samaria and killed their priests.

setting.body: Bethel lay in the former kingdom of Israel, an Assyrian province after 722. Guzik notes that Assyria's weakness made the intervention possible; ABC 3 shows Assyria fighting for survival against Babylon and the Medes from 616.

constraints.textual_assertion: Josiah took away … and did to them according to all the acts that he had done in Bethel
assumptions: Kings places the Bethel actions within the reform narrative; their year is not stated.

competing_reconstructions.label: Prophecy of 1 Kgs 13:2 fulfilled
competing_reconstructions.summary: See the prophecy record for the traditional and critical readings.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik calls Josiah's act the remarkable fulfilment of the prophecy of 1 Kgs 13:1–2 and notes that Josiah honoured the anonymous prophet's grave.

open_questions: How far Josiah's control extended into the province of Samaria (2 Chr 34:6 adds Naphtali).
No excavation report for Iron Age Bethel was read.
